title: Week 9 - SSDs
content: ## What? NAND flash memory-based drives. They are based on NAND flash cells. - Each flash cell can hold 1-5 bites. - Cells on a chip are organized into pages. - Multiple pages are organized into erase blocks They support: - Reading a page. - Fast. Happen at the granularity of pages. - Writing to an erased page - 10x slower than reads. Happen at the granularity of pages. - Erasing a block - 10x slower than writes. Happen at the granularity of erase blocks. ## Pros vs. Cons ### Pros SSDs have the following advantages over disks: - much faster than hard drives - support random access - more resilient against physical damage - reduced power consumption ### Cons - Flash memory is written in pages, but erased in blocks. **It can become fragmented and needs GC!** - *Flash memory can only be erased / written a fixed number of times* - Wear leveling trying to balance writes over blocks ## Architecture SSD maintains a map of LBNs to pages. ### Writes Block storage devices expose storage as linear array of logical blocks - These blocks are unrelated to flash erase blocks OS issues a write with data D to LBN A: 1. If the page corresponding to LBN A is non-empty, it does NOT overwrite but rather finds an erased page to write D and the LBN A page is GC later. ### Wear Levelling - Dynamic wear leveling - Controller spreads new writes across blocks that have the lowest erase counts - Static wear levelling - The controller occasionally relocates long-lived (“static”) data out of low-wear blocks into higher-wear blocks. Frees the low-wear blocks so they can take future writes. *Dynamic wear leveling only affects frequently written data. Static data can remain in low-wear blocks forever, so static wear leveling moves it to ensure all blocks age evenly.* #### Write Amplification - **The number of actual writes to the device is larger than the number of writes the OS issues to the device.** - Caused by GC and wear levelling. WAF = # bytes written to flash chips / # bytes issued to device by OS Minimize WAF: - sequential - large writes - no overwrites ### Garbage Collection Unless there is a write in the same spot, controller doesn't know which LBA's it can GC. There is a special SATA command TRIM that allows the OS to tell the SSD that specific LBAs are invalid and may be GCed.
